data.value: “{0}” is the “Take over” sink: redirected apps play there too, so they will be heard twice

data.value: the sink device wasn’t found (unplugged or removed)

data.name: Sink_VaioOffFormat
data.value: “{0}” is a Voicemeeter VAIO input, and Voicemeeter isn’t running: such an input doesn’t accept streams and hangs the Windows Audio service

data.name: Sink_ProbeFailedFormat
data.value: “{0}” failed the check: {1}

data.name: Sink_IsDefaultFormat
data.value: “{0}” is the default device: people listen to it, and apps in “Take over” mode will be heard directly

data.name: Sink_VaioUnreliableFormat
data.value: “{0}” is an unreliable sink: it works only while Voicemeeter is running. A separate VB-Cable is recommended

data.name: Sink_FewerChannelsFormat
data.value: the sink has {0} ch. and the default device “{1}” has {2}: if an app doesn’t reopen its stream when the device changes, Windows downmixes it to {0} ch. with normalization, and it gets quieter (by up to {3:0.0} dB). Setting the sink format to {2} ch. helps (“Sound” → device → “Configure”), or restarting playback in the app
data.comment: {0} = sink channels, {1} = default device, {2} = its channels, {3} = loss in dB
